name: Semiconductor and electronics
tagline: Small but growing door; far fewer real jobs this year than the headlines promise

door_size.caveat: Minister's Aug 2026 statement of 50,000 to 60,000 direct jobs 'in coming years' spread over roughly four years; only 3 of 12 approved units are in production, 85,000 engineers have already been trained under C2S, and the earlier NLB projection of 1 million jobs by 2026 did not materialise.

pay_band.note: Design-services firms and ATMP/OSAT plants pay 4 to 6 for most freshers; NVIDIA 22 to 30, Qualcomm 17 to 23, Intel and Broadcom 16 to 22 go to a small number, mostly M.Tech or tier-1 B.Tech. Source is a low-confidence salary guide.

tiers_realistic.tier1: Yes. Qualcomm, NVIDIA, Texas Instruments, Micron, Samsung and AMD run campus drives at IITs, NITs and IIITs, and prefer M.Tech VLSI for design roles; B.Tech offers go mainly to the top of the ECE class.
tiers_realistic.tier2: Partly. Design-services firms (Tessolve, eInfochips, Sankalp, MosChip, HCLTech and Wipro engineering units) and the new fabs and OSATs (Tata Electronics, Micron Sanand, CG Semi, Kaynes) hire B.Tech ECE/EE from tier-2 colleges, usually through off-campus tests and their own training programmes; pay starts in the 4 to 6 band.
tiers_realistic.tier3: Hard but not closed, and honesty matters here: about 1.6 lakh students enrol in ECE each year (supply.aicte.branch_enrolment.ece.2024_25) against a door of tens of thousands at most, so most tier-3 ECE graduates will not get a VLSI design job in two years. What substitutes for the brand: a C2S-supported college licence for Cadence or Synopsys tools with a finished RTL-to-GDS or verification project you can defend, a GATE ECE score (useful for M.Tech VLSI, ISRO and PSU routes), and a willingness to start in test, product engineering, DFT or fab/ATMP operations rather than front-end design. A paid VLSI training institute is not required; free NPTEL and C2S material plus a real project is a stronger signal than a certificate.

entry_requirements: Digital design fundamentals: combinational and sequential logic, FSMs, timing, CMOS basics; tested in every screening
Verilog or SystemVerilog to the level of writing and simulating a module (FIFO, UART, AXI-lite slave) with a testbench; open-source Icarus/Verilator or Cadence Xcelium via a C2S college licence
For verification roles (the largest fresher intake in design services): SystemVerilog and UVM basics, assertions, coverage
For back-end roles: static timing analysis, synthesis, place-and-route concepts, DFT basics (scan, ATPG, BIST) and familiarity with Synopsys or Cadence flows

For fab, ATMP and OSAT roles (Tata Electronics, Micron, CG Semi, Kaynes): semiconductor process basics, statistics and SPC, cleanroom discipline, shift work; Chemical and Mechanical graduates also enter here
Programming for scripting and automation: Python and TCL, plus Linux; C for embedded and post-silicon validation
M.Tech VLSI or a GATE ECE score for the higher-paying design houses; a 7+ CGPA filter at Qualcomm, NVIDIA, TI and Micron campus drives

two_year_plan.title: Digital design and Verilog, with free tools
learn: NPTEL 'Digital Circuits' and 'Hardware Modeling using Verilog' (IIT Kharagpur, free)
Verilog and SystemVerilog basics on open-source tools: Icarus Verilog, Verilator, GTKWave; HDLBits for daily practice

Get access to your college's C2S (Chips to Startup) licences for Cadence or Synopsys; if your college is not on C2S, ask the ECE department to apply and use open-source OpenROAD and SkyWater 130 nm PDK meanwhile
Python and Linux shell for scripting; basics of TCL
Start GATE ECE preparation alongside (networks, signals, digital, EDC) since it opens M.Tech VLSI, ISRO and PSU doors
build: A parameterised FIFO and a UART transmitter/receiver in Verilog with self-checking testbenches, on GitHub
evidence: GitHub repos with waveforms in the README
target: Nothing yet; use this half to decide between design/verification and fab/ATMP tracks based on what you enjoy

two_year_plan.title: Verification (UVM) or physical design; first RTL-to-GDS
learn: SystemVerilog for verification and UVM: free Verification Academy (Siemens) courses, Doulos tutorials, ChipVerify
Synthesis and STA concepts: setup and hold, clock domains, constraints (SDC); NPTEL 'VLSI Physical Design' (IIT Kharagpur)
DFT basics: scan insertion, ATPG, BIST; read the Synopsys or Cadence DFT user guide sections your C2S licence covers
Complete an RTL-to-GDS flow once on OpenROAD/OpenLane with SkyWater 130 nm, then repeat on Cadence Genus/Innovus via C2S if available
build: A UVM testbench for your UART or an AXI-lite peripheral with functional coverage and assertions
An RTL-to-GDS run of a small RISC-V core or your own design with timing closed and a DRC-clean layout
evidence: Coverage report and bug list from the UVM project
GDS screenshot, timing report and area numbers in the README
target: VLSI internships (summer): Tessolve, eInfochips, Sankalp, MosChip, Samsung SSIR and Qualcomm intern postings
Flipkart-style hiring challenges do not exist here; apply directly on career pages and via faculty referrals

two_year_plan.title: Internship or fab/ATMP entry, and the evidenced project
learn: If you got a design-services internship: the company's flow, scripting for regressions, reading a spec end to end

If not: semiconductor manufacturing basics for the fab and OSAT track (NPTEL 'Semiconductor Device Fabrication'; Micron and Tata Electronics operator-to-engineer pathways), plus six-sigma and SPC basics
Post-silicon validation and test (ATE basics, bench debugging) which is where Tessolve's TET programme and TI's test roles start
GATE ECE mock tests weekly if you are keeping the M.Tech or ISRO route open
build: The evidenced project below (an automotive-grade CAN or LIN controller IP with full verification and DFT)
evidence: Internship completion letter or a fab/ATMP trainee offer
Project repo with verification plan, coverage closure and DFT report
target: Tata Electronics early careers (Dholera fab, Jagiroad ATMP, Hosur)
Micron Sanand and Hyderabad new-college-grad roles
ISRO ICRB Scientist/Engineer SC (Electronics), CBT Oct 2026

two_year_plan.title: Interviews across design, DFT, test and manufacturing
learn: Interview drill: FSM design on a whiteboard, setup/hold arithmetic, CDC, FIFO depth calculation, UVM phase questions, scan chain questions
Read two public datasheets end to end and explain the register map; interviewers test whether you can read a spec
Prepare a 30-minute walkthrough of the evidenced project and a one-page summary of the internship or trainee work
build: Portfolio page listing the three builds with reports; keep applying weekly to design services, OSATs and product companies' new-grad postings
target: Qualcomm, NVIDIA, TI, AMD, Micron new-college-graduate postings (2026 and 2027 batches)
M.Tech VLSI at an NIT or IIT via GATE as the alternative door; fallback to ev_automotive embedded roles

evidenced_project_spec.title: Automotive CAN 2.0B controller IP: RTL, UVM verification and DFT
evidenced_project_spec.scope: Design a CAN 2.0B controller (bit timing, arbitration, CRC, error handling, TX/RX message buffers with an AXI-lite register interface) in Verilog; write a verification plan and a UVM testbench with a CAN bus model, functional coverage and assertions; synthesise, run STA, insert scan and generate ATPG patterns; run RTL-to-GDS on SkyWater 130 nm with OpenROAD or on Cadence tools through a C2S licence. Target use case: a body-control ECU in a two-wheeler EV.
evidenced_project_spec.agent_use: A coding agent drafts the register map documentation, generates the UVM skeleton, scripts regressions and produces first-pass testbench sequences from the CAN specification; the graduate writes the RTL and the assertions by hand, reviews every generated sequence against the spec, and records the cases where the agent misread the standard (for example bit-stuffing rules). A research agent is used to summarise ISO 11898-1 timing requirements, which the graduate verifies against the standard text.
evidenced_project_spec.done_looks_like: RTL passes a regression of at least 200 randomised tests with 95%+ functional coverage and zero open bugs; timing closed at 100 MHz on the target library; scan coverage above 95% with ATPG patterns; DRC/LVS-clean GDS; a 10-page design document with block diagram, register map, verification plan, coverage report, timing summary and DFT summary.
evidenced_project_spec.verification: Regression and coverage reports committed to the repo and reproducible with one script; an independent check by interoperating with an open-source CAN model (or a second student's implementation); a faculty or industry reviewer signs off on the verification plan; the graduate can explain for 30 minutes how arbitration is verified, one real bug the testbench caught, why scan coverage was not 100%, and what changed between RTL and post-layout timing.

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Write testbench boilerplate, sequences and regression scripts by hand
ai_task_shift.now: Agents generate UVM skeletons, sequences and regression scripts from a spec; verification engineers spend more time on the plan and the coverage holes
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Verification planning, deciding what to cover, reading the spec correctly, and debugging the failures the generator cannot explain

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Hand-write RTL for standard blocks (FIFOs, arbiters, bus interfaces)
ai_task_shift.now: Agents produce first-draft RTL for standard blocks; quality varies and must be checked against timing and area
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Micro-architecture, power and timing trade-offs, and reviewing generated RTL for synthesisability and corner cases

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Iterate synthesis, placement and timing closure by manually tuning constraints and scripts
ai_task_shift.now: EDA vendors ship AI-driven flow optimisation (Synopsys DSO.ai-style and Cadence Cerebrus-style tools) that explore settings automatically
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Setting the constraints and goals, judging when a result is real versus an artefact, and signing off tape-out risk

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Read datasheets and standards and summarise them for the team
ai_task_shift.now: Agents summarise standards in minutes, sometimes wrongly
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Verifying the summary against the source, and the engineering judgement about what the standard means for this design

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Fab and ATMP process monitoring by reading charts on shift
ai_task_shift.now: Anomaly detection and yield analytics flag excursions automatically
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Root-cause analysis, process changes, equipment ownership and the shift decisions that cost real money if wrong

fit_rules.reason: ECE is the core branch for design, verification, DFT and test roles.
EE graduates are hired on the same terms as ECE for VLSI and for fab equipment roles.
Fab process and ATMP roles at Tata Electronics, Micron and CG Semi take Chemical and Materials graduates.
There is no realistic entry for Civil graduates in this path.
Only software roles at chip companies are open, and those compete with CS graduates; chip design needs an ECE/EE base.
The high-paying design houses run campus drives at IITs, NITs and IIITs and prefer M.Tech VLSI from them.
Design houses rarely visit tier-3 colleges; the realistic entry is design services, test, or fab/ATMP operations, or M.Tech via GATE.
Bengaluru and Hyderabad hold most design and verification jobs.
Gujarat (Dholera fab, Sanand ATMP and OSATs) is where the new manufacturing jobs are.
Tata's Jagiroad ATMP in Assam is the first large semiconductor employer in the North-East.
Jobs are in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Sanand, Dholera and Jagiroad; you need to be able to move.
Unless home is Bengaluru, Hyderabad or near Sanand, there are almost no semiconductor jobs near home.
Design and verification roles take 12 to 24 months of preparation for a tier-2/3 graduate; fab/ATMP trainee roles are faster but shift-based.
A year of runway allows the project work or GATE attempt this path needs.
This path is circuits and chips every day.
Entry-level semiconductor work is deep technical work with little customer contact.
Slow entry and a 4 to 6 lakh starting band for most; only a few reach the 16 to 30 band.
Verilog/VHDL and EDA tool experience is exactly what screeners look for.
GATE ECE opens M.Tech VLSI, ISRO and PSU routes, which are the main tier-2/3 entries to design roles.
If you enjoyed labs and hardware, the daily work here will suit you.
